We empirically determine an approximate thousand-fold improvement in the probability of finding a state close to the ground state for these instances, over implementation without an XX interaction.
item.dc:creator: Robert J. Banks, Natasha Feinstein, Roopayan Ghosh, Sebastian Schulz, Kristel Michielsen, Sougato Bose, P. A. Warburton

item.title: No advantage from classical assistance for energy-constrained bosonic dephasing channels
item.description: arXiv:2610.13854v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that four capacities of single-mode bosonic dephasing channels coincide under an average photon-number constraint: the unassisted quantum capacity, the unassisted private capacity, the two-way classically assisted quantum capacity, and the two-way public-classically assisted private capacity. The assistance may be interactive: the parties can exchange classical messages between channel uses and choose subsequent inputs based on earlier outcomes. For every finite value of the constraint, their common value is the coherent information optimized over Fock-diagonal input states satisfying the constraint. The proof uses a relative entropy comparison with the completely dephasing channel to derive chain rules for the Rains relative entropy and the relative entropy of entanglement. These chain rules give an upper bound on the rates achievable by adaptive protocols whose mean input photon number is constrained on average over all channel uses. We also show that both chain rules are attained by canonical purifications of finite-energy Fock-diagonal states.
item.dc:creator: Amir Arqand, Graeme Smith

item.title: GPU-Based Parallel BP Decoding for Quantum LDPC Memory
item.description: arXiv:2610.13879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) decoding requires reliable corrections and low latency over long syndrome histories. We extend BP-SF, an oscillation-guided belief-propagation (BP) decoder with independent syndrome-flip trials, by introducing windowed and streaming operations. Our CUDA implementation combines disordered-memory retries, sliding windows, correlation-aware graphs, and layered scheduling. Circuit-level simulations test fixed-basis memory and complete logical Pauli-frame recovery. On the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle code at physical error rate p = 0.002, parallel BP-SF reduces 99.9th-percentile call latency by a factor of 13.15 relative to an eight-chain Relay-BP GPU baseline on 100,000 matched samples for which every tested method's initial BP stage fails within 80 iterations. Windowed BP-SF maintains a flat logical error rate and nearly constant per-round compute time through 512 rounds, reaching a 17.1-fold speedup over monolithic decoding. In 512-round full-frame streaming decoding with 2.97-ms syndrome arrivals, layered BP-SF on a transformed joint graph with 20 retries reduces 99.9th-percentile correction-release age from 166.29 to 36.25 ms relative to the joint graph with flooding updates and 100 retries. These results connect parallel BP post-processing to lower decoding costs and earlier correction release in streaming quantum memory.
item.dc:creator: Ming Wang, Yanbo Zhao, Ang Li, Frank Mueller

item.title: Bicycle Race: small two-block codes on the Pareto frontier
item.description: arXiv:2610.13880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-block group-algebra codes are among the simplest quantum LDPC codes, and many of them are translation invariant on a twisted torus, which suits neutral-atom arrays and other platforms with movable qubits. We ask how far they go at small sizes when searched systematically across all groups. To tackle this question, we use a series of algebraic constraints and screens to design a search pipeline capable of enumerating broad and complete swathes of two-block codes on a laptop. With it we census about $10^8$ two-block codes with up to $320$ qubits at check weights five to nine. Several of these censuses are exhaustive, and support complete statements; for instance, the Gross code is, up to equivalence, the only abelian weight-six two-block code with $n \le 200$ to reach $kd^2/n=12$, and the known $[[64,18,8]]$ is the best two-block code by $kd^2/n$ across weights five to nine with $n \le 94$. The censuses are also large enough to give insights into where good codes live - they concentrate in a handful of groups; abelian groups give the best codes at small $n$ and non-abelian groups at large $n$, with the crossover appearing to move out as the check weight grows; and high quality codes become $100$ to $1000$ times rarer per draw from weight six to weights eight and nine. Using the group algebra and the census data to steer a statistical search finds four to fifteen times as many good codes as uniform draws in equal time. Among the codes found are $[[102,20,10]]$ and $[[120,24,10]]$ at check weight nine, which we simulate in noisy syndrome-extraction circuits, and $[[288,16,16]]$, the best weight-six two-block code with $n \le 300$. At check weights seven to nine, our best codes exceed the best published $kd^2/n$ with exact distance at the same check weight in most length bands up to $320$ qubits. All codes are available in a public database.
item.dc:creator: Gideon Lee

item.title: An Annealing-based Quantum Neural Network with Discrete Wavelet Transforms for Enhanced Air Pollution Nowcasting
item.description: arXiv:2610.13882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Air pollution poses a significant threat to public health, exacerbated by the rapid industrialization and urbanization of modern society. While traditional deep learning offers predictive capabilities, recent advancements in quantum machine learning (QML) present a compelling alternative. Here, we introduce a scalable hybrid framework that integrates variational quantum circuits with quantum annealing. Leveraging a neuromorphic quantum computing platform to transcend the qubit limitations of the NISQ era, we model particulate matter (PM$_{2.5}$) dynamics using high-density urban data from the UK. We demonstrate that our Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) exhibit an intrinsic resilience to input volatility, significantly outperforming classical baselines (MLP and LSTM) on raw, high-entropy environmental data. Furthermore, we successfully scaled the model to 172 qubits, observing a synergistic enhancement when coupled with wavelet decomposition that achieves state-of-the-art predictive fidelity. These findings establish a critical benchmark for quantum utility, proving that scalable, neuromorphic quantum machine learning can now address complex, non-linear real-world problems.
item.dc:creator: Otto Menegasso Pires, Andr\'e Saimon, Daniela Herrmann, Prashant Kumar, Marcelo Moret, Erick Giovani Sperandio Nascimento

item.title: Maximally antiflat fixed-particle-number fermionic states
item.description: arXiv:2610.13903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fermionic Gaussian states are completely characterized by their two-point correlations, making the covariance matrix a natural reference for quantifying non-Gaussian structure. Motivated by fermionic antiflatness, we study its extremal form for pure number-conserving states and ask which states can be maximally antiflat and how they can be constructed. We show that, at fixed particle number, maximal first antiflatness is equivalent to a completely flat one-body reduced density matrix, and we obtain a complete existence classification together with explicit block and cyclic-orbit constructions of all allowed sectors. We then investigate the structure that appears beyond the covariance level. Maximally antiflat states with identical one-body data can exhibit distinct connected four-point correlations, which we characterize through the four-point Majorana Wick error and, equivalently, the connected two-body reduced density matrix cumulant. We show that this quartic structure is necessarily nonzero and formulate its extremization as a two-body reduced density matrix (2RDM) purity problem. Combining this framework with a Hilbert--Schmidt estimate of Christiansen for truncated two-body correlations, we obtain an upper bound on the connected quartic structure in terms of first antiflatness. Our results establish both a complete characterization of maximal fermionic antiflatness at fixed particle number and a constrained hierarchy linking covariance-level flatness to higher-order non-Gaussian correlations.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Gupta, Arya Haghighian, James D. Whitfield

item.title: Quantum Query Complexity of Maximum Degree and its Generalizations
item.description: arXiv:2610.13906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the quantum query complexity of several basic graph problems. 1) We prove a tight $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ bound for finding a maximum-out-degree vertex in an $n$-vertex tournament, resolving a conjecture of Mande, Paraashar, and Saurabh [FSTTCS'23]. 2) Using the same proof idea, we give a direct proof that finding a maximum-degree vertex in an $n$-vertex undirected graph requires $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ quantum queries, a bound implicit in the work of Apers and Lee [CCC'21]. Both lower bounds above hold even for computing only the maximum degree or maximum out-degree. 3) We also study Maximum $(k,n-k)$-Cut, which asks for the largest cut with one side of size $k$. For every constant $k\geq 1$, we give an $O(n^{2-1/(k+1)})$-query quantum algorithm. 4) We establish a reduction to Maximum $(k,n-k)$-Cut involving $k$-Graph Collision, which asks whether the marked vertices of a known graph contain a $k$-clique. For $k\geq 3$, this yields unconditional lower bounds with exponents strictly larger than $3/2$, showing that this problem is strictly harder than computing maximum degree. Additionally, under a conjecture we propose for $k$-Graph Collision, the reduction yields a lower bound matching our upper bound above.
item.dc:creator: Amin Shiraz Gilani, Nikhil S. Mande, Subhasree Patro, Nithish Raja

item.title: A scalable sample-based quantum diagonalization solver for general Pauli-sum Hamiltonians
item.description: arXiv:2610.13907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A scalable ground-state solver to be used in sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) is presented. The solver is built on JAX API, and is intended to be run on GPU platforms and possibly many-GPU high-performance computing facilities. It is capable of subspace diagonalization in up to $2^{30}$-dimensional subspace, with possible upgrades to enable even larger-scale operations. The two main components, a general-purpose eigensolver and an SQD-specific matrix-vector operation function, are described in detail. Efficiency of the eigensolver with respect to the GPU memory is demonstrated using a simple physics model. Furthermore, good strong scaling of the eigensolver in many-GPU environment is observed.
item.dc:creator: Yutaro Iiyama

item.title: A Warped Born Rule Turns an Observer into a Maxwell's Demon
item.description: arXiv:2610.13936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum mechanics seems to be an incredibly delicate theory. Slight alterations to nearly any part of its structure can lead to huge qualitative differences and wildly unphysical predictions. Here, we explore the many-body consequences of replacing the Born rule $p(m)\propto\|P_m|\psi \rangle|^2$ by a warped rule $p_b(m)\propto\|P_m|\psi\rangle\|^{2b}$. Specifically, in systems with conserved particle number, evolution punctuated by repeated local particle observations acquires a probabilistic bias over measurement histories with an effect controlled by the sign of $b-1$. For $b>1$, this bias generically drives the gas to collect into nearly frozen configurations. Similar to the action of Maxwell's demon, the simple act of observation seems to extract entropy from a closed system. For $b<1$, the bias is reversed, generically scouring out long-wavelength fluctuations to produce a hyperuniform gas. We study this effect in a one-dimensional quantum gas, where these two phases are derived analytically for a particular measurement scheme and corroborated numerically for more general procedures with discrete-time projective-measurement circuit models using matrix product state simulations. We additionally discuss how this bias manifests in a common technique that often employs this warped rule, the ``replica trick,'' implying qualitative differences between finite-replica and replica-limit calculations.
item.dc:creator: Olumakinde Ogunnaike

item.title: An entangling Hubbard quasiparticle collider on a digital quantum processor
item.description: arXiv:2610.13946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scattering of quasiparticles provides direct access to the interactions that govern strongly correlated systems. In this work, we realize the quasiparticle scattering experiment of the Fermi-Hubbard model on a digital quantum processor by colliding a doublon and a holon in the half-filled chain of 21 sites encoded on 42 qubits of the ibm_boston processor. For the first time, we measure the transmission probability of quasiparticles of the Hubbard model on quantum hardware, which agrees with the Bethe-ansatz scattering matrix without free parameters. Beyond the scattering probabilities, the collision generates entanglement by superposing the transmitted and reflected components, which we infer from the particle-number fluctuation. In sharp contrast, a control collision between two doublons shows neither the interaction dependence nor the number fluctuation, as expected for indistinguishable particles. Our work demonstrates that the ability to create quasiparticles of a chosen flavor on demand and program their motion and interactions makes a digital quantum processor a new experimental toolset for probing the entanglement structure generated by quasiparticle scattering.
item.dc:creator: Chan Bin Bark, Hanbyul Kim, Yoonil Koo, SeungBeom Hong, Seik Pak, Kwang Jun Ahn, Sangmo Cheon, Youngseok Kim, Moon Jip Park

item.title: Exchange-controlled quantum beats and entanglement in an exciton--bimodal-cavity system
item.description: arXiv:2610.04111v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We theoretically demonstrate tunable population transfer and entanglement generation in a two-exciton system coupled to a bimodal optical cavity, including an exciton-exciton exchange interaction. By using dressed-state transformations and L\"{o}wdin partitioning, we derive effective Hamiltonians that identify three dynamical time scales: local polaritonic oscillations, long-period dressed-state beats, and direct excitonic exchange. We apply the framework to graphene nanoribbon excitons, using excitonic energies, transition dipoles, and lifetimes obtained from first-principles calculations to parameterize the model. In the small- and moderate-exchange regimes, the dynamics become multiscale, and the beat channel sustains sizable quantum entanglement over long dissipative time windows. In the large-exchange regime, the excitonic Hamiltonian dominates and drives nearly complete population transfer between excitonic states over many coherent cycles. The resulting analytical expressions provide direct design rules connecting the beat period, transfer amplitude, and coherent-cycle number to the exchange interaction, cavity detuning, and light--matter coupling. Our results establish a controllable route for engineering long-lived entanglement and coherent excitonic operations in exciton--bimodal-cavity systems.
item.dc:creator: Cesar E. P. Villegas, Victor P. Brasil, Pedro A. S. Contri, Kevin Liz\'arraga, Jonas Maziero

item.title: Frustrated Topological Orbital Magnetism
item.description: arXiv:2610.12557v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: By studying the interplay of geometric frustration with Aharonov-Bohm fluxes in three dimensions, we unveil a rich playground exhibiting topological semimetallic ground states with orbital magnetic dipole, quadrupole and ferrotoroidic orders, akin to spin patterns in classical spin ices - a class of phenomena which we dub frustrated topological orbital magnetism. We demonstrate that the ground-state toroidizations underpinned by non-Abelian topological nodal lines induce measurable current-induced Hall phenomena. We further find that distinct 2-in-2-out and 3-in-1-out frustrated orbital current patterns can be associated with topological Weyl node charges, and corresponding anisotropic linear and nonlinear Hall effects. We propose signatures for experimental validation of distinct frustrated topological orbital magnetic orders in candidate materials.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Garrido Bourkhaeva, Claudio Castelnovo, Wojciech J. Jankowski

item.title: An elementary approach to the Szeg\H{o} theorems
item.description: arXiv:2610.12724v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The strong Szeg\H{o} theorem and the Fisher-Hartwig formula describe the asymptotic behavior of determinants obtained by restricting translationally invariant operators to large finite regions. In particular, Szeg\H{o}'s theorem states that, beyond the leading extensive contribution to such a determinant, there is a universal finite correction, $\sum_{r>0} rV_rV_{-r}$ where $V_r$ are the Fourier coefficients of the logarithm of the symbol. Although this formula appears throughout analysis and mathematical physics, the origin of its quadratic form and of the weight $r$ is often obscured in its standard analytic derivations. We develop an elementary picture in which the strong Szeg\H{o} term arises from boundary leakage: paths contributing to the matrix exponential leave the finite interval and subsequently return. Counting the shortest such excursions immediately produces the factor $r$. We then show that an isolated boundary contributes exactly one half of the strong Szeg\H{o} correction, while the two boundaries of a long interval decouple. For finite-range matrices this gives a rigorous and intuitive elementary derivation of the asymptotics, with extensions to sufficiently rapidly decaying interactions. A complementary free-fermion argument provides a physical interpretation of the same cancellation mechanism. Numerical examples illustrate the asymtotics in the well controlled regime, the Fisher Hartwig logarithmic correction. The boundary formulation does not itself require translation invariance and therefore suggests natural extensions to disordered systems, higher dimensions, and symbols with internal matrix structure. To illustrate this we numerically go beyond the formal applicability region of the Szeg\H{o} formula, considering slow decay and disordered cases, and showing in some cases a robustness of the approach even for slowly decaying but disordered potentials.
item.dc:creator: Israel Klich, Ravisankar Rajagopal

item.title: Lieb-Robinson bounds for irreversible dynamics via adaptive Dyson expansion
item.description: arXiv:2610.12731v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note, we study a broad class of time-dependent and irreversible dynamics for quantum spin systems in both finite and infinite volume. We develop a simple and flexible strategy for expanding commutators of the form $[A,\tau_{s,t} \, B]$ in terms of self-avoiding paths of sets, where $A$ and $B$ are local operators and $\tau_{s,t}$ is the Heisenberg time evolution. This adaptive Dyson expansion requires no backwards time evolution and is thus also applicable to irreversible dynamics. Furthermore, we discuss how such an expansion directly implies Lieb-Robinson bounds. A central feature of our result is that the obtained Lieb-Robinson bounds are independent of any Hamiltonian and dissipative on-site terms of the generator.
item.dc:creator: Carla Rubiliani, Marius Wesle, Tom Wessel

item.title: Distinguishing Flat and Warped Extra Dimensions with Unruh-DeWitt Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2610.13016v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We examine the response of a two level Unruh-DeWitt (UD) detector interacting with the Kaluza-Klein (KK) mass modes of a bulk scalar field in extra dimensional models. Considering two of the promising extra dimensional models with distinct compactifications, such as large, flat extra dimensions in the Arkani Hamed, Dimopoulos \& Dvali (ADD) framework and warped extra dimensions in the Randall-Sundrum (RS) scenario, we compute the profile function of the detector. We extend this computation to the 6 dimensional doubly compactified spacetime geometry. The profile function of the detector has been examined as a function of the energy gap of the detector, the compactification radius of the extra dimension, and the dimensionality of spacetime, requiring the chosen parameter space appropriately such that the gauge hierarchy problem is duly addressed. We find that the pattern of the profile function is dictated by the spacing of the KK mass spectrum and the resolution of the detector. For ADD model, the spacing between successive KK modes decreases with the increasing compactification radius, yielding a smoothly increasing continuum pattern in the profile function. Whereas for the RS warped geometry model, a tiny deviation in the radius of the extra dimension produces a large change in the same, resulting a sharp increment. The resolvability of the KK mode structure is sensitive to the underlying geometry of the spacetime, providing a qualitative distinction between flat and warped extra dimensional scenarios within the UD detector framework.
item.dc:creator: Ashmita Das, Anjana Krishnan, Soumitra Sengupta

item.title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
item.description: arXiv:2610.13084v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. Notably, in the extreme quantum limit at cryogenic temperatures, the magnetoresistance undergoes a dramatic reversal from negative to positive. This reversal points to a potential field-induced phase transition into a collective electronic state driven by enhanced electron-electron interactions. Our findings provide valuable insights into the unconventional chiral transport and emergent correlated quantum states under extreme magnetic fields.
item.dc:creator: Zhifeng Xue, Jiaji Zhao, Yi Ji, Fuyang Chen, Nannan Tang, Gangjian Jin, Bing Shen, Bin Wang, Yang Wang, Mingxi Chi, Jin-Zhu Zhao, Ruiqiang Wang, Qizhong Zhu, He Wang, Huakun Zuo, Donghui Guo, Dingyong Zhong, Mingxun Deng, Huichao Wang

item.title: Real Fiducial Vectors Only Exist in Dimensions $d\equiv 3 \pmod{4}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.13168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate restrictions on the dimensions and coordinate fields of real Weyl-Heisenberg fiducial vectors. Our main result is that such vectors can exist only in dimensions $d\equiv 3\pmod{4}$. This result is motivated by evidence showing that real Weyl-Heisenberg fiducial vectors can exist only in dimensions $d = 4m^2 + 3, m \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. We further restrict the possible dimensions when the coordinate field is a totally real number field, an even or odd degree extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, a real quadratic field, or a maximal real subfield of a cyclotomic field. Lastly, we establish non-existence over odd-degree number fields under either positivity of all non-trivial cyclic-shift overlaps or a conjectural containment of a distinguished quadratic field in the SIC field.
item.dc:creator: Igor Van Loo, Fr\'ed\'erique Oggier

item.title: Graphene double quantum dot as a solid-state two-level system in the THz range
item.description: arXiv:2610.13196v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Matter-based two-level quantum systems are fundamental building blocks of quantum technologies, underpinning applications in quantum computing, simulation, communication, and sensing. Today, most of these two-level quantum systems, including Rydberg atoms, trapped ions, superconducting circuits, molecules, and quantum dots, involve transition frequencies in microwave or optical domains. However, extending their transition frequency to the THz spectral range could provide numerous benefits, leveraging the unique properties of THz radiation. Here, we show that an hBN-encapsulated graphene double quantum dot realizes a two-level system with a transition frequency in the THz spectral range. Using low-temperature transport spectroscopy in the dark combined with modeling based on nonequilibrium Green's function formalism, we demonstrate the formation of an artificial molecule, featuring bonding and antibonding states separated by an energy of up to 0.6 meV, corresponding to a resonance frequency of 0.145 THz. This approach provides direct access to important parameters of open double quantum dot systems, including tunneling rates, offering a practical alternative to conventional techniques such as photon-assisted tunneling, which are challenging to implement at THz frequencies. The realized 2D-material-based THz two-level system, compatible with direct on-chip integration, could serve as a key building block for future THz quantum technologies. Furthermore, by involving a single-electron transition, coupling these devices to a THz resonator could enable the exploration of ultra-strong light-matter interactions at the fundamental limit of a single transition coupled to a single cavity, beyond the reach of existing THz quantum systems based on collective transitions.
item.dc:creator: Alexis Wietzke, Solen Coeymans, Benjamin Hue, Simon Messelot, Aurelien Schmitt, Michael Rosticher, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Jerome Tignon, Sukhdeep Dhillon, Rebeca Ribeiro, Audrey Cottet, Matthieu Delbecq, Takis Kontos, Juliette Mangeney

item.title: Theory of exciton-exciton interactions in crystalline systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13246v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Excitons are bound electron-hole pairs in semiconductors whose interactions influence optical properties and determine their collective behavior and emergent correlated phases. Despite the theoretical and experimental significance of these phenomena, a microscopic theory of exciton-exciton interactions that takes into account the full composite nature of these quasiparticles is lacking. Here, we present a general theory of exciton-exciton interactions that builds upon our previous publication [Physical Review B 113, 155440 (2026)], which applied only to conventional semiconductors with weak band hybridization. By contrast, the theory presented here is valid in virtually any crystalline semiconducting system and can be applied to the study of biexciton formation and correlated excitonic phases in systems where band topology, quantum geometry, and moir\'e effects play a significant role. In addition to the analytical theory, we also present results in simple systems with flat bands with a nontrivial quantum metric and show that the biexcitonic spectrum differs strongly from that in the case without quantum geometry. Our theory paves the way for accurate quantitative calculations of biexciton spectra and excitonic many-body phases in modern condensed-matter systems.
item.dc:creator: L. Maisel Licer\'an, H. T. C. Stoof

item.title: Second quantization and compactness of induced Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize compactness of the Hilbert-Schmidt semigroups induced by finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful normal invariant state. A unitary second-quantization representation for every $ s $-embedding shows that compactness at one positive time, compact resolvent, drift stability, and uniqueness of the normal invariant state are equivalent. These conditions imply immediate trace-class membership for all embeddings. We derive exact trace-norm and Hilbert--Schmidt norm formulas, an embedding-independent trace identity, and the generator spectrum with algebraic multiplicities. Examples show that compactness does not require the existence of a spectral gap and that a spectral gap need not imply compactness when the invariant state is not unique.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Li

item.title: Holographic Krylov complexity in confining backgrounds: particle, string, and frames
item.description: arXiv:2610.13555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate holographic Krylov complexity in bottom-up holographic QCD models describing the confined phase, using the recently proposed correspondence between the growth rate of Krylov complexity and the proper radial momentum of probes, such as particles and strings, falling in the bulk spacetime. As representative confining backgrounds, we consider two horizonless geometries, namely the dilaton-deformed AdS-soliton and the deformed thermal-AdS spacetime, both arising as solutions of an Einstein-dilaton gravity system. We find that the Krylov complexity associated with a massive particle exhibits qualitatively distinct behavior in these two backgrounds when analyzed in the Einstein frame. In the deformed AdS-soliton geometry, the complexity undergoes periodic oscillations, with both the oscillation period and amplitude depending on the parameters of the model. In contrast, in the deformed thermal-AdS geometry, the complexity grows exponentially at late times and does not display oscillatory behavior. We then investigate string dynamics in the string frame and find that the Krylov complexity exhibits oscillatory behavior in both confining backgrounds. This behavior is traced to the emergence of an additional turning point in the deep infrared of the string-frame geometry. Motivated by this observation, we further analyze massive-particle dynamics in the string frame, where we find qualitatively similar behavior in the two confining backgrounds. Our results demonstrate that the Krylov complexity of confined holographic systems depends sensitively on the choice of probe and frame, while also revealing a closer correspondence between the two confining geometries in the string-frame description.
item.dc:creator: Jasper Nongmaithem, Deepak Kumar Kar, Ayush Kumar, Shreeya Rajesh Parab, David Dudal, Subhash Mahapatra

item.title: Replica Transition at Measurement-Altered Ising Criticality
item.description: arXiv:2610.13802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Performing measurements on gapless quantum ground states can give rise to new universal phenomena, whose origins remain poorly understood even for the paradigmatic Ising critical point. Replica methods offer a natural framework to study such post-measurement ensembles, with the replica limit $Q\to 1$ describing physical Born-averaged observables. Here we show that, for the monitored critical Ising chain, the replicated post-measurement ensemble of states itself undergoes a phase transition precisely at the physically relevant replica limit $Q \to 1$, preventing standard replica treatments. We use boundary conformal field theory (BCFT) methods to explain the underlying mechanism of this transition. Our methods yield a perturbative analytic calculation of the universal $O(1)$ constant in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record, previously known only numerically. We also apply our tools to study measurement-averaged spin correlators, providing a unified description of the universal properties of measurement outcomes and post-measurement states in the critical Ising chain.
item.dc:creator: Kabir Khanna, Sara Murciano, Romain Vasseur

item.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
item.description: arXiv:2610.13811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong results in classical code generation and are increasingly used to write the unit tests that safeguard that code. Whether they can do the same for quantum software is less clear, because quantum programs are probabilistic, depend on numerical tolerances, and are judged by domain-specific checkers, so a well-formed test can still disagree with the benchmark's verdict. Existing quantum benchmarks measure whether a model produces a correct solution, but not whether its tests can distinguish correct implementations from faulty ones. We introduce QTestBench, a framework that evaluates LLM-generated quantum test suites against independent benchmark checkers, never treating the tests themselves as ground truth. For each task, QTestBench prompts models to produce syntactic, semantic, and behavioral tests, injects candidate solutions at runtime, and compares each test verdict with the checker's label under three validation cohorts, each answering a distinct diagnostic question. We benchmark five LLMs on eight PennyLane QHack challenges and ten Qiskit HumanEval tasks. Generated suites almost always execute, but discrimination lags behind: the best generator reaches a test quality of 0.71 on QHack and 0.34 on Qiskit HumanEval, so executability alone overstates test quality. Oracle-verified synthetic mutants stabilize bug-detection estimates when natural faulty solutions are scarce, as on three of ten Qiskit tasks that yield none. QTestBench offers a reproducible, cross-framework benchmark for the trustworthiness of LLM-generated quantum tests.
item.dc:creator: Meriem Terki, Nouhaila Innan, Minghao Shao, Muhammad Kashif, Alberto Marchisio, Muhammad Shafique

item.title: Proof of a Universal Speed Limit on Fast Scrambling in Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2404.15403v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the time required for sustained information scrambling in any Hamiltonian quantum system is universally at least logarithmic in the entanglement entropy of scrambled states. This addresses two foundational problems in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics. (1) It sets the earliest possible time for the applicability of equilibrium statistical mechanics in a quantum system coupled to a bath at a finite temperature. (2) It proves a version of the fast scrambling conjecture, originally motivated in models associated with black holes, as a fundamental property of quantum mechanics itself. Our result builds on a refinement of the energy-time uncertainty principle in terms of the infinite temperature spectral form factor in quantum chaos. We generalize this formulation to arbitrary initial states of the bath, including finite temperature states, by mapping Hamiltonian dynamics with any initial state to nonunitary dynamics at infinite temperature. A regularized spectral form factor emerges naturally from this procedure, whose decay is universally constrained by analyticity in complex time. This establishes an exact speed limit on information scrambling by the most general quantum mechanical Hamiltonian, without any restrictions on locality or the nature of interactions.
item.dc:creator: Amit Vikram, Laura Shou, Victor Galitski

item.title: Exponential entanglement advantage in sensing correlated noise
item.description: arXiv:2410.05878v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Correlated noise naturally arises in quantum systems due to, e.g., phase and amplitude fluctuations in global control or long-range correlations generated by a many-body sensing target near criticality. In this Letter, we propose a new form of exponential quantum advantage in the context of sensing correlated noise. Specifically, we focus on the problem of estimating parameters associated with Lindblad dephasing dynamics, and show that entanglement enhancement in the sensitivity (as quantified via quantum Fisher information of the sensor state) arises for estimating the strength of fluctuations in the noise fields' center-of-mass mode. In the presence of strong background fluctuations, such enhancement grows exponentially with the number of probes in the shot-limited regime, when the measurement and reset operations are slow. This result stands in stark contrast with previously studied scenarios of sensing uncorrelated dephasing noise, where one can prove that entanglement does not lead to an advantage in the signal-to-noise ratio. Our work thus opens a novel pathway towards achieving entanglement-based sensing advantage, which may find applications in characterizing decoherence dynamics of near-term quantum devices. Further, our approach provides a potential quantum-enhanced probe of many-body correlated phases by measuring noise generated by a sensing target. We also discuss realization of our protocol using near-term quantum hardware.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Xin Wang, Jacob Bringewatt, Alireza Seif, Anthony J. Brady, Changhun Oh, Alexey V. Gorshkov

item.title: Erasing Photon-Number Correlations through Hong-Ou-Mandel Interference
item.description: arXiv:2502.06570v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A parametric down-conversion source interfering on a beam splitter can be described as both a source of entangled N00N-states or a source of independent, and thus uncorrelated squeezers. The disparity between these outcomes can be attributed to whether one takes a standard discrete- or continuous-variable approach to describing the system. More precisely, this difference in output is due to the types of measurements involved and the way in which the data is processed, as both setups are identical, clearly identical states are produced. Here we take a hybrid approach to describe the state, which is generated by parametric down-conversion as input state, and investigate the measurements of the output ports of the interferometer using photon number resolved detection. We show that the output of this interference is separable in the photon number picture and demonstrate the worth of photon-number correlation measures for the characterization of squeezed light sources for hybrid applications like Gaussian boson-sampling.
item.dc:creator: Fabian Schlue, Patrick Folge, Takefumi Nomura, Philip Held, Federico Pegoraro, Michael Stefszky, Benjamin Brecht, Stephen M. Barnett, Christine Silberhorn

item.title: Fundamental limits for thermodynamic control with quantum feedback
item.description: arXiv:2503.09012v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The study of feedback control inspired by Maxwell's demon has yielded fundamental insights into the relationship between thermodynamics and information. However, its fully quantum formulation, where the controller holds quantum side information that cannot be treated as a classical record, remains incomplete. In this paper, we establish fundamental no-go limits for thermodynamic state conversion while allowing quantum side information to be fed back to the system coherently. From two basic operational principles respected by all physically admissible feedback-control schemes, we derive the tightest possible bounds on the single-shot work of formation and extractable work for arbitrary quantum systems conditioned on arbitrary quantum side information. In the asymptotic limit, these bounds yield a generalized second law of thermodynamics with quantum feedback, governed by a conditional free energy. We further show that this generalized second law is consistent with the traditional second law once the acquisition, processing, and reset of side information are accounted for. These results extend information thermodynamics to the fully quantum regime and provide precise thermodynamic meanings for the negativity of single-shot conditional entropies.
item.dc:creator: Kaiyuan Ji, Gilad Gour, Mark M. Wilde

item.title: Physics-inspired Generative AI models via real hardware-based noisy quantum diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2505.22193v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum Diffusion Models (QDMs) are an emerging paradigm in Generative AI that aims to use quantum properties to improve the performances of their classical counterparts. However, existing algorithms are not easily scalable due to the limitations of near-term quantum devices. Following our previous work on QDMs, here we propose and implement two physics-inspired protocols. In the first, we use the formalism of quantum stochastic walks, showing that a specific interplay of quantum and classical dynamics in the forward process produces statistically more robust models generating sets of MNIST images with lower Fr\'echet Inception Distance (FID) than using totally classical dynamics. In the second approach, we realize an algorithm to generate images by exploiting the intrinsic noise of real IBM quantum hardware with only four qubits. Our work could be a starting point to pave the way for new scenarios for large-scale algorithms in quantum Generative AI, where quantum noise is neither mitigated nor corrected, but instead exploited as a useful resource.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Parigi, M., Martina, S., Venturelli, F.A. et al. Physics-inspired Generative AI models via real hardware-based noisy quantum diffusion. Quantum Mach. Intell. 8, 110 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Marco Parigi, Stefano Martina, Francesco Aldo Venturelli, Filippo Caruso

item.title: Superconducting-antiqubit simulation enables optimal phase estimation via unitary inversion
item.description: arXiv:2506.04315v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A positron is equivalent to an electron traveling backward through time. Casting transmon superconducting qubits as akin to electrons, we simulate a positron with a transmon subject to particular resonant and off-resonant drives. We call positron-like transmons "antiqubits." An antiqubit's effective gyromagnetic ratio equals the negative of a qubit's. This fact enables us to time-invert a unitary implemented on a transmon by its environment. We apply this platform-specific unitary inversion, with qubit--antiqubit entanglement, to achieve a quantum advantage in phase estimation: consider measuring the strength of a field that points in an unknown direction. An entangled qubit--antiqubit sensor offers the greatest possible sensitivity (amount of Fisher information), per qubit, per application of the field. We prove this result theoretically and observe it experimentally. This work shows how antimatter, whether real or simulated, can enable platform-specific unitary inversion and benefit quantum information processing.
item.dc:creator: Xingrui Song, Surihan Sean Borjigin, Flavio Salvati, Yu-Xin Wang, Nicole Yunger Halpern, David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur, Kater Murch

item.title: High-throughput bidirectional electro-optic transduction assessed with a practical quantum capacity
item.description: arXiv:2507.09873v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A microwave-optical transducer of sufficiently low noise and high signal transfer rate would allow entanglement to be distributed between superconducting quantum processors reliably within the lifetimes of their quantum memories. We report the continuous operation of an efficient transducer at high enough bandwidth to realize kHz signal transfer rates, in downconversion as well as upconversion, with noise levels approaching that required for quantum information transfer. To define the significance of our advance and clarify the multifaceted performance required for quantum networking tasks, we derive a broadband quantum channel capacity that bounds the maximum rate at which quantum information can be sent through realistic finite-bandwidth thermal-loss channels. This capacity serves as a comprehensive measure of transducer capability and provides insight into the relative importance of disparate performance metrics. We find that the broadband capacity depends on the throughput---defined as the product of efficiency, bandwidth, and duty cycle---and on the added noise. We present measurements of a membrane-based opto-electromechanical transducer with high throughput of 7 kHz and at an input-referred added noise of 3 photons in both upconversion and downconversion, demonstrating that bidirectional transducer capacities comparable to superconducting qubit decay rates are within reach. In downconversion, throughput of this magnitude at the few-photon noise level is unprecedented, marking an improvement of nearly four orders of magnitude over previous work.
item.dc:creator: M. D. Urmey, S. Dickson, K. Adachi, S. Mittal, L. G. Talamo, A. Kyle, N. E. Frattini, S. -X. Lin, K. W. Lehnert, C. A. Regal

item.title: Finite-Size Effects in Quantum Metrology at Strong Coupling: Microscopic vs Phenomenological Approaches
item.description: arXiv:2507.19994v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Equilibrium quantum metrology is often formulated under assumptions of weak system-bath coupling and thermodynamic limit scaling, which may not be valid for realistic finite-size (FS) quantum devices. Here, we establish how strong coupling (SC) and FS effects jointly modify achievable precision bounds for equilibrium quantum probes. Considering a transverse-field anisotropic XY spin chain coupled to a thermal environment, first utilize we derive a full polaron transform to derive the effective Hamiltonian at equilibrium. Then, using the bare Hamiltonian and the obtained effective Hamiltonian and taking into account the role of FS effects in the calculation of partition function, we derive an analytic expressions for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for a general parameter for the equilibrium state in weak coupling (WC) and SC regimes, respectively. In contrast to this microscopic approach, we also utilize the Hill's phenomenological nanothermodynamics to calculate an effective QFI expression at SC. Our results, presented for specific cases of magnetometry and thermometry, reveal that considering FS and SC effects lead to substantial and systematic deviations in QFI, even for moderate system sizes, and that commonly used thermodynamic-limit approximations can significantly misestimate precision. This work also highlights the inadequacy of phenomenological approaches in describing the metrological capability and thermodynamic behavior of systems at SC. Our work establishes a consistent framework for evaluating metrological performance of realistic, finite quantum devices operating beyond the weak-coupling paradigm.
item.dc:creator: Ali Pedram, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl{\i}o\u{g}lu

item.title: Noise Thresholds for Quantum Advantage in the Bernstein-Vazirani and Deutsch-Jozsa Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2508.01884v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analytically investigate the robustness of the Bernstein-Vazirani and Deutsch-Jozsa algorithms against single-qubit Pauli noise, of which bit-flip, phase-flip, and depolarizing noise are special cases, using the density-matrix formalism. For a general Pauli channel acting on each qubit after every gate, we derive exact closed-form expressions for the success probability of a single run as a function of the error probabilities and the number of qubits $n$, and validate them against Qiskit simulations. The noise enters only through the probability $\varepsilon$ with which each output bit is flipped. Under bit-flip noise with error probability $p > 1/2$ the most probable outcome of the Bernstein-Vazirani algorithm is the complement of the correct one, which classical post-processing corrects, whereas depolarizing and phase-flip noise never bias the output toward a wrong outcome. For the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm, the success probability is the average over constant and balanced oracles, and the results are given for the single-variable balanced oracle, which is shown to be the least robust of all balanced oracles for $\varepsilon < 1/2$. For a single run, the tolerable error probability of both algorithms decreases as $1/n$. We then determine the minimum number of repetitions required for a given confidence and compare it with the number of queries of the classical algorithms. The threshold error probability below which the noisy Bernstein-Vazirani algorithm retains its query advantage increases with $n$, whereas that of the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm with its standard readout decreases as $1/n$. This contrast indicates that algorithms whose answer is encoded in many independently decodable output bits are considerably more robust to noise than algorithms whose verdict depends on a single global outcome.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Faizan, Muhammad Faryad

item.title: Classical and Quantum Heuristics for the Binary Paint Shop Problem
item.description: arXiv:2509.15294v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Binary Paint Shop Problem (BPSP) is an $\mathsf{APX}$-hard optimisation problem arising in automotive manufacturing: given a sequence of $2n$ cars, comprising $n$ distinct models each appearing twice, the task is to decide which of two colours to paint each car so that the two occurrences of each model are painted differently, while minimising consecutive colour swaps. Performance is measured by the paint swap ratio -- the average number of colour changes per car -- which directly affects production efficiency and cost. Prior work showed that the Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) at depth $p=7$ achieves a ratio of $0.393$, outperforming the then-best-known classical heuristic, Recursive Greedy, with a proven asymptotic expected ratio of $0.4$ [Phys. Rev. A 104, 012403 (2021)]. More recently, the Recursive Star Greedy (RSG) heuristic was proposed with a conjectured expected ratio of $0.361$. Here, we formally reduce BPSP to weighted MaxCut, yielding an exact Ising formulation, and benchmark two state-of-the-art low-depth QAOA variants -- eXpressive QAOA and Recursive QAOA -- at $p=1$ (denoted XQAOA$_1$ and RQAOA$_1$) against four classical BPSP heuristics. Across instances ranging from $2^7$ to $2^{12}$ cars, XQAOA$_1$ achieves an average paint-swap ratio of $0.357$; in our instance-wise benchmarks, it outperforms RQAOA$_1$ on almost all instances and each of the four classical baselines, including RSG, on every instance. Surprisingly, RQAOA$_1$ deteriorates with problem size despite employing provably near-optimal QAOA$_1$ parameters at each recursive step, eventually falling behind RSG at the largest sizes. To our knowledge, this is the first report of size-dependent performance degradation of RQAOA$_1$ at scale. In contrast, XQAOA$_1$ remains stable across all tested sizes, with no evidence of size-dependent degradation.
item.dc:creator: V Vijendran, Dax Enshan Koh, Ping Koy Lam, Syed M Assad

item.title: Entanglement thresholds for sequential nonlocality sharing in star networks
item.description: arXiv:2512.13357v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum networks promise scalable distributed quantum information processing. Realizing this potential depends critically on the efficient use of nonclassical resources. Sequential sharing of quantum nonlocality provides a resource-efficient route for recycling entanglement across multiple observers. In network settings, however, such recycling is typically constrained by a trade-off between the number of active branches and the achievable sharing depth. Here we investigate this problem in star networks using probabilistic projective measurements. We establish an explicit entanglement threshold above which nonlocality can be shared across all branches up to any target depth, and below which we determine the optimal trade-off between the number of active branches and the achievable number of sequential rounds. We further analyze the protocol's robustness to noise and its experimental observability, clarifying its practical feasibility. These results establish quantitative design principles and entanglement requirements for scalable nonlocality recycling in quantum networks.
item.dc:creator: Ming-Xiao Li, Yuqi Li, Rui-Bin Xu, Mo-Ran Zhu, Haitao Ma, Chang-Yue Zhang, Zhu-Jun Zheng

item.title: Scalable and telecom single-erbium system with record-long room-temperature quantum coherence
item.description: arXiv:2601.11879v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Achieving long-lived ({\mu}s-scale) quantum coherence at room temperature in the telecom C band remains a central unsolved challenge for solid-state quantum platforms, with coherence at this timescale previously demonstrated only under vacuum cryogenic conditions at temperatures over 600 times lower. To this end, we introduce a CMOS-compatible nanoengineering approach that deterministically controls the number of Er ions within a nanoscale volume and their electromagnetic environment using sub-5 nm silicon-based hollow nanopillars, which achieves the first deterministic spatial isolation of single erbium ions. This nanostructure-enabled isolation suppresses ion-ion interactions and local electromagnetic field noise, enabling single-erbium-ion operation under ambient conditions. The resulting individually addressable single-ion devices exhibit record room temperature optical coherence times of T2*= 32 {\mu}s and T2 > 100 {\mu}s in the telecom C-band. We further present the first demonstration of background-free, upconversion-enabled single photon emission from multilevel erbium qudits, providing high contrast coherent optical readout. Beyond these performance gains, our work, through sub-5-nm nanoscale engineering, establishes isolated single-ion environments as a viable route to room-temperature operation for solid-state quantum systems. This approach has the potential to address the long-standing barrier of room-temperature decoherence and open a manufacturable, telecom-compatible pathway toward scalable quantum networks, distributed sensing, and cryogenic-free quantum photonic integrated circuits.
item.dc:creator: Alex Kaloyeros, Natasha Tabassum, Spyros Gallis

item.title: Quantum Approximate Optimization for Decoding of Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
item.description: arXiv:2602.21124v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Decoding Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes is a fundamental problem in coding theory, and Belief Propagation (BP) is one of the most popular methods for LDPC code decoding. However, BP may encounter convergence issues and suboptimal performance, especially for short-length codes and in high-noise channels. The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is a type of Variational Quantum Algorithm (VQA) designed to solve combinatorial optimization problems by minimizing a problem-specific cost function. In this paper, we present a QAOA-based decoding framework for LDPC codes by formulating a decoding cost function that incorporates both parity-check constraints and soft channel reliability information. The resulting optimization problem is solved using QAOA to search for low-energy configurations corresponding to valid codewords. We test the proposed method through extensive numerical experiments and compare its performance with BP decoding. The experimental results demonstrate that the QAOA-based decoder achieves a higher probability of correctly recovering the transmitted codeword than BP across multiple experimental settings.
item.dc:creator: Krishnakanta Barik, Goutam Paul

item.title: Operator dynamics in k-Markov random circuits
item.description: arXiv:2603.18217v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate that $k$-Markov sequences of unitary gates provide low-cost handles to manipulate the rate and structure of information spreading compared to traditional random, 0-Markov, circuits. For SWAP gates and brickwork circuits, we use graph cover time to demonstrate how $k$-Markov processes can be used to control operator transport. With SWAP gates and the set of Clifford gates that can change operator weight, we show how $k$-Markov sequences can be used to manipulate scrambling time and generate novel structures of spatial-temporal correlations across a qubit network. We show that $k$-Markov circuits constructed from PSWAP gates at fixed angle are equivalent to standard brickwork circuits with PSWAP angle drawn from non-uniform distributions generated by the $k$-Markov process. In those circuits, the time evolution of the average Hamming weight and the space-time correlation structure that remains after one-point quantities equilibrate again vary significantly from the 0-Markov case, depending on the transition probabilities of the process. More broadly, these results identify finite temporal memory as a control handle distinct from a circuit's degree of quantum chaos. For gate sets that fall short of volume-law scrambling, the equilibrium reached by one-point diagnostics is fixed by the gates alone, while the choice of $k$-Markov rule controls the approach to equilibrium and the structure of persistent, late-time correlations.
item.dc:creator: Unnati Akhouri, Pei-Jun Huang, Elliott Rose, Sarah Shandera

item.title: Optimizing Entanglement Distribution Protocols: Maximizing Classical Information in Quantum Networks
item.description: arXiv:2603.25360v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large-scale quantum networks depend on the efficient distribution of entangled pairs between distant nodes. However, state-of-the-art solutions rely on restrictive operational assumptions, incur prohibitive computational complexity, and optimize metrics misaligned with application needs. This paper addresses the entanglement distribution problem introducing four pivotal advances. First, since the primary application of quantum communication is private information transmission, we derive the Ensemble Capacity, a novel metric that quantifies the private classical information enabled by entanglement distribution. Second, we propose a generalized formulation of the Entanglement Distribution Problem that allows arbitrary sequencing of entanglement swapping and purification, removing the structural restrictions of prior models. Third, to navigate the resulting combinatorial space, we introduce a dynamic programming-based hypergraph generation algorithm that preserves exact, continuous fidelities, avoiding quantization, while pruning sub-optimal sequences in advance. Finally, we integrate these solutions into CODE, a two-tier orchestration framework enabling near-real-time network operation. Extensive evaluations show that our approach achieves higher private information capacity and significantly lower computational complexity than existing solutions, while meeting the sub-second latency requirements of dynamic quantum network operation.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Sanchez Hidalgo, Diego Zafra Bono, Guillermo Encinas Lago, J. Xavier Salvat Lozano, Jose A. Ayala-Romero, Xavier Costa Perez

item.title: Mixed eigenstates in spin-boson systems with one-photon and two-photon interactions
item.description: arXiv:2604.05037v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spin-boson systems have attracted increasing attention as accessible experimental platforms and for their potential applications in designing quantum technologies. One characteristic of these systems is the transition from regular to completely chaotic behavior when certain control parameters are varied. However, the characterization of their mixed phase space has not been thoroughly explored. In this work, we investigate the properties of mixed eigenstates in spin-boson systems, comparing one-photon interactions with two-photon interactions. We propose a generalized definition of the phase-space overlap index to identify genuine mixed eigenstates. Our study highlights the fundamental differences that arise when two-photon processes are considered compared to one-photon processes and provides complementary evidence supporting the validity of the principle of uniform semiclassical condensation of quasiprobability functions in spin-boson systems.
item.dc:creator: David Villase\~nor, Marko Robnik

item.title: Borns Rule from Reversible Evolution and Irreversible Outcomes
item.description: arXiv:2604.07418v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the quadratic measure associated with the Born rule need not be introduced as an independent probabilistic postulate, but follows, under the stated structural and regularity assumptions, from the compatibility between reversible linear evolution and the formation of stable records. Physical processes alternate between reversible dynamics and episodes of record formation. Quantities that remain well defined throughout such processes must therefore admit a representation that remains consistent across both regimes. Prior to record formation, alternatives combine additively at the level of complex amplitudes, whereas successive record-forming distinctions admit a multiplicative representation through refinement. Requiring compatibility between these compositional structures constrains the admissible weight assignment to the family of weights proportional to the pth power of the amplitude magnitude. The finite-dimensional specialization of Lamperti's isometry theorem then singles out p = 2 as the unique value compatible with continuous reversible linear mixing while preserving total weight. The Born rule therefore emerges as the unique weight assignment compatible with reversible linear composition, multiplicative record refinement, phase invariance, and continuous reversible invariance, without invoking probabilistic assumptions or a specific interpretation of quantum measurement.
item.dc:creator: Oskar Axelsson

item.title: Adaptive Window Decoding based on Spatiotemporal Complementary Gap
item.description: arXiv:2605.14637v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Real-time decoding plays a crucial role in practical fault-tolerant quantum computing. Window decoding, in which the decoding problem is divided into windows, is a promising approach. While reducing the window size is desirable for faster decoding, each window contains a buffer region whose size must typically be at least the code distance to avoid degrading the logical error rate, which limits how much the window can shrink. In this paper, we propose an adaptive decoding scheme in which window decoding is first performed with a small buffer size and a decoding confidence (soft information) is computed; if the confidence is low, the buffer size is enlarged and decoding is redone. This approach reduces the average decoding time, since most shots are decoded with a small buffer. A central challenge in realizing this scheme is that existing forms of soft information are not directly applicable to window decoding, especially with a small buffer. We address this challenge by introducing a new form of soft information, the spatiotemporal complementary gap, specifically designed for this setting. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed scheme reduces the average buffer size by approximately 40% while maintaining the logical error rate. Beyond the reduction of average decoding time, the proposed method is also expected to contribute to reducing the reaction time for non-Clifford operations and relaxing the hardware requirements for real-time decoding.
item.dc:creator: Moeto Mishima, Riki Toshio, Kaito Kishi, Jun Fujisaki, Hirotaka Oshima, Shintaro Sato, Keisuke Fujii

item.title: Multi-flux Aharonov-Bohm caging with tunable couplings
item.description: arXiv:2605.23546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Aharonov-Bohm (AB) caging is the complete wavefunction localization effect in translational-invariant lattices induced by destructive phase interference. These phases originate from the gauge fields such as the penetrated magnetic fields, which are directly related to several novel topological quantum states of matter. Recently, this effect has shown significant potential for applications in quantum simulation and topological quantum computation. Here, we propose a scalable protocol to derive universal conditions for AB caging with multi-flux. The numerical simulations validate the theoretical predictions by directly observing AB caging phenomena. We also investigate the breakage of the caging effect with onsite detuning, decoherence and non-Hermitian transitions. Our protocol provides an alternative approach for advancing quantum simulation of exotic states of matter.
item.dc:creator: Le-Chuan Wang, Sai Li, Jia Liu, Zheng-Yuan Xue

item.title: Lie Algebra-Based Quantum Optimal Controls Interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2606.02014v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a framework combining Lie group theory and feed-forward neural networks to efficiently generate quantum optimal control pulses for arbitrary unitary operations in superconducting qubit systems, bypassing the need for explicit optimization at inference time. The exponential scaling of the Hilbert space dimension with qubit number makes standard optimization approaches computationally prohibitive when large ensembles of distinct propagators must be processed, a bottleneck that is particularly acute in Trotterized quantum simulation. Our method addresses this limitation by pre-computing a representative set of control pulses via Lie group theory and training neural networks to map target propagators to their corresponding pulses. We demonstrate the approach on superconducting qubit systems of 2, 3, and 4 qubits, finding high reconstruction fidelity for specific combinations of Lie algebra parameters. As a physically motivated benchmark, we apply the methodology to reconstruct control pulses for the Trotter propagators of a neutrino system undergoing collective flavor oscillations. The successful generalization across system types demonstrates that a single model -- trained once on hardware-specific random propagators -- can serve as a universal control-pulse generator for any target quantum system of compatible Hilbert space dimension, offering a promising route toward scalable quantum simulation.
item.dc:creator: Piero Luchi, Francesco Pederiva

item.title: Certified Bounds on the Measurement Cost of Molecular Hamiltonians
item.description: arXiv:2607.16866v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum estimates of molecular energy require repeated state preparation and measurement. We bound the minimum repetition count for given measurements and processing rules from above with a practical schedule and from below with independently verified inequalities. For an H$_4$ chain at H-H distances of 0.90 and 1.80 \AA with 2 per cent uniform noise in the ground state, entangling Clifford measurements, which map Pauli products onto one another, cut leading-order repetitions by at least 65.9 and 61.0 per cent, respectively, relative to any schedule using only single-qubit Pauli measurements and Hamiltonian terms. With 69 unaltered measurement settings, each a basis change followed by qubit readout, processing further observables saves at least 12.04 and 6.70 per cent. For four lanthanide and actinide Hamiltonians with depolarized Hartree-Fock covariances, reducing the sum of absolute Hamiltonian coefficients does not proportionally reduce sampling. The bounds cover linear unbiased estimates from independent batches at small error.
item.dc:creator: Federico Zahariev, Vanda Glezakou

item.title: Beyond Orbital Rotations: Correlation-Rank Limits and Clifford-Accessible Measurement, from Algebra and Global Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2607.16869v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: One should not assume that reconstructing an electronic observable with a smaller set of measurement settings will cut the number of repetitions in proportion. Each setting is simply a basis change and qubit readout, but the savings are not guaranteed to be commensurate. Take two electrons of opposite spin in two spatial orbitals: the orbital degree of freedom of each electron acts as a logical qubit and rotations are independent in the spin sectors. From the observable's one- and two-qubit coefficients we derive an exact floor for the setting count and a decomposition to meet it in no more than three settings. With fewer settings, the minimum error in the two-qubit correlation coefficients is set by the singular values left out. A case in point is an exchange with equal nonzero couplings on the three Pauli axes. This demands three orbital settings yet only one joint measurement. We offer a Clifford circuit for four physical qubits to effect the necessary mapping of Pauli products under conjugation. In the case of a one-parameter family of logical singlet-triplet mixtures, the orbital-to-Clifford shot cost ratio is three at maximum mixing and trends toward 3/2 near the logical singlet. Where spin sectors may be mixed, isotropic exchange needs one orbital setting. For spin-conserving Hamiltonians with $N$ spatial orbitals encoded via Jordan-Wigner, the $X$-rank, the binary rank of the $X$ parts of its strings, of any commuting Pauli string family is no more than $2(N-1)$. Searches with the Robust Adaptive Nature-inspired Global Explorer (RANGE) reach this limit for CH$_4$, with the rank of the Hamiltonian support vouching for the maximality of the search values. And for all nonidentity Pauli strings on $n$ qubits, semidefinite witnesses from the Lov\'asz theta number give a lower bound on the Clifford setting count that agrees with the integer cover and counting bounds at $2^n+1$.
item.dc:creator: Federico Zahariev, Vanda Glezakou

item.title: Equivariant Continuous Normalizing Flows with Offline Sampling for Fermionic Ground State Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2607.18486v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a framework for fermionic variational Monte Carlo in which a continuous normalizing flow refines a fixed antisymmetric base wavefunction. The flow is a permutation-equivariant neural ordinary differential equation (ODE), a smooth, topology-preserving map; equivariance preserves the antisymmetry of the base, so the flow can in principle improve any antisymmetric ansatz that can be sampled efficiently. The flow deforms the nodal surface of the base but cannot change its topology, so the base must supply the correct nodal topology. We use Slater and Jastrow-Slater bases in this work. Exact samples from the flow's Born distribution are obtained by pushing pre-cached base samples through the forward ODE, requiring no Markov chain Monte Carlo at training time. Base samples are generated offline and reused across batches and runs, enabling embarrassingly parallel training across multiple GPUs. We introduce three permutation-equivariant vector field architectures, Pairwise Deep Sets, FermiNet Vector Fields, and Pairwise Deep Sets Gradient, each balancing expressivity and computational cost differently. We further introduce an augmented dynamics formulation that co-evolves the derivatives required for the kinetic energy as ODE state variables, eliminating differentiation through the ODE trajectory and significantly reducing wall-clock time and memory. On harmonically trapped spinless electrons, the flow reaches ground-state energies below configuration interaction with single and double excitations, on par with a FermiNet baseline trained with the same optimizer. Training shows near-ideal strong scaling to 128 NVIDIA A100 GPUs on NERSC's Perlmutter for the largest systems tested, up to $N = 48$ particles in three dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Sam Cochran, James B. Larsen, James Stokes, Andrew Wray, Michael J. Keiser, Chad Rigetti, Shravan Veerapaneni

item.title: Purcell-Engineered Hybrid Coupler for Leakage-Suppressed Robust CZ Gates
item.description: arXiv:2607.23463v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a Purcell-engineered notch-filter hybrid coupler for superconducting controlled-$Z$ (CZ) gates that combines coherent interaction engineering with leakage-selective dissipation. The architecture integrates a nonlinear transmon coupler with a coupled Purcell-filter and notch-resonator subsystem, providing additional control over both the coherent interaction pathways and the engineered dissipative environment. The filter branch reshapes the effective interaction pathways, while the notch resonator further tailors the frequency response of the coupled filter network and preserves strong leakage-selective dissipation. Using dressed-eigenstate analysis together with Lindblad master-equation simulations, we show that the proposed architecture substantially reduces leakage and retains high-fidelity, low-leakage operation compared with an optimized single-transmon coupler while remaining robust over a broad range of coherence assumptions and device parameters. The gate analysis reconstructs the projected computational quantum channel and therefore retains the phase information required to distinguish a CZ operation from identity. The nominal operating point occurs at $t_{\rm CZ}=327.46~\mathrm{ns}$ with $F_{\rm avg}^{\rm CZ}=99.714\%$, $L_{\rm avg}=8.78\times10^{-4}$, and $L_{\rm max}=2.04\times10^{-3}$. A minimax timing-robust operating point at $327.20~\mathrm{ns}$ maintains $F_{\rm avg}^{\rm CZ}\geq99.590\%$ over a $\pm0.50~\mathrm{ns}$ timing window. These results demonstrate that engineered dissipation complements conventional coherent interaction engineering and provides an additional design degree of freedom for realizing robust, high-fidelity superconducting CZ gates.
item.dc:creator: Hui Wang, Feng Bao, Yan-Jun Zhao, Xun-Wei Xu

item.title: DC Conductance of X-shaped Majorana Interferometer reveals Non-Abelian Anyon Statistics
item.description: arXiv:2607.24171v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a four-terminal, X-shaped chiral Majorana interferometer with a central floating superconducting island, enabling the direct detection of the non-Abelian statistics of Ising anyons via the linear-response DC conductance tensor in charge transport experiments. Here, Ising anyons are realizable as edge vortices nucleated at Josephson line junctions defining the superconducting island, where both edge-vortex and Majorana-fermion tunneling processes can occur. We show that in such a multi-terminal Majorana interferometer, both the vacuum and the fermionic fusion channel for Ising anyons are possible. This is in contrast to two-arm interferometers, where only the vacuum fusion channel is accessible and the DC conductance contribution from edge vortices always vanishes. Using a low-energy effective theory derived via chiral bosonization, we find that in the X-shaped interferometer, the DC conductance tensor is completely isotropic, yielding a non-zero conductance when simultaneous edge-vortex and Majorana tunneling activates the fermionic fusion channel. Apart from conductance oscillations in a gate-tunable charge parameter, which display an offset related to the anyon topological spin, measuring a finite conductance can already provide direct evidence for non-Abelian statistics in this geometry.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Giuliano, Andrea Nava, Reinhold Egger, Fabian Hassler

item.title: Reinforcement Learning to Harness Approximation Errors for Long-Time Quantum Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2608.20139v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate digital quantum simulation at long times is limited by the accumulation of errors inherent to approximate simulation. Here we introduce RL-Trotter, a reinforcement-learning framework that treats unavoidable approximation errors as resources for error correction rather than merely imperfections to suppress. We show that low-dimensional information from conservation laws, such as the energy and energy variance, provides a sufficient learning signal to guide the agent, which learns to adapt a single scalar---the next Trotter step size---without access to the target wave function. By optimizing the entire long-time evolution rather than individual steps, RL-Trotter discovers self-correcting sequences in which later errors compensate for those accumulated earlier, increasing the accuracy of the long-time dynamics. The learned policies are intrinsically robust to measurement noise, substantially reducing measurement overhead. They also generalize to previously unseen, physically similar initial states and transfer from small, classically simulable systems to systems an order of magnitude larger. This enables a practical protocol based on classical pretraining followed by direct deployment or limited fine-tuning on quantum hardware. Our results establish a broader perspective for quantum algorithms: errors in approximate evolution can be orchestrated into resources for accurate and resource-efficient quantum dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Bo Shi, Markus Heyl, Roderich Moessner, Marin Bukov, Hongzheng Zhao

item.title: Sharp State-Independent Uncertainty Relations for Multipartite systems
item.description: arXiv:2608.22656v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Uncertainty relations constrain the fluctuations of incompatible observables, but most familiar bounds depend on the quantum state. State-independent uncertainty relations instead ask how much fluctuation remains unavoidable for every quantum state. For observables generated by a continuous symmetry, sharp state-independent bounds are known when the symmetry representation is irreducible. Multipartite collective systems, however, generally appear as reducible tensor-product representations of a symmetry algebra, which raises the question of how to determine their total uncertainty. We resolve this problem for multipartite quantum systems with a compact semisimple symmetry algebra $\mathfrak g$. Exploiting the symmetry structure, we formulate a general framework for state-independent uncertainty based on representation theory. The total variance admits an exact decomposition into intrinsic fluctuations within irreducible sectors and a nonnegative dispersion between sectors. This yields the sharp state-independent bound for the total variance $\Delta_\rho^2(\mathfrak g)$ on the multipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ \[ \min_{\rho}\Delta_\rho^2(\mathfrak g) = \min_{\lambda\in\Lambda(\mathcal H)} 2\langle\lambda,\delta\rangle, \] where $\rho$ is any density operator on $\mathcal H$, $\Lambda(\mathcal H)$ is the set of highest weights $\lambda$ labeling those sectors, and $\delta$ is the Weyl vector. This demonstrates that the ultimate uncertainty is completely controlled by its intrinsic symmetry structure. As an application of the general theory, we confirm our previous conjecture [JPA 59, 155302 (2026)] that the total uncertainty floor of collective spin-$1/2$ systems depends only on the parity of the particle number. We further illustrate the framework for multipartite spin-$1$ systems, demonstrating that the same symmetry-sector mechanism persists beyond spin-$1/2$.
item.dc:creator: Yiling Wang, Naihuan Jing

item.title: Efficient Quantum Simulation of Linearized Vlasov--Poisson Dynamics Using Trotter and THRIFT Hamiltonian Simulation Methods
item.description: arXiv:2608.23127v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Vlasov--Poisson system provides the fundamental kinetic description of plasma and plays a central role in understanding collective phenomena such as Landau damping and wave--particle interactions. Efficient numerical simulation of these dynamics remains challenging because of the high dimensionality of phase space. In this work, we studied magnetized and non-magnetized plasma using a quantum simulation framework for the linearized Vlasov-Poisson equation by reformulating the discretized system as a Hermitian Hamiltonian suitable for gate-based quantum computation. The time evolution is implemented using first, second and fourth-order Trotter--Suzuki product formulas and the recently proposed Time-Resolved Interaction Framework (THRIFT).
